Evidence: The Karnataka government has issued an advisory stating that people should only visit hospitals in case of an emergency. This directive is aimed at preventing crowding and the spread of COVID-19. The advisory specifies that patients with mild illnesses requiring outpatient care or follow-up should not visit hospitals for the next two weeks or until further notice (Source 1, Source 2, Source 3).
Justification: The retrieved evidence clearly indicates that the Karnataka government is urging people not to visit hospitals unless it is an emergency. This directly contradicts the claim that the government is encouraging visits for non-emergency care. The advisory explicitly states that only patients requiring emergency care may visit hospitals, thus refuting the claim.
